html:
SMTO-SKL-0091 — SMTO couldn't open the local page Microsoft sign-in returns to

GUID: c0f6b1ce-720a-5f75-b92d-78ecc3f0aee4
Slug: microsoft365-oauth-listener-unavailable
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • Microsoft sign-in sends you back to a small page that SMTO opens on the computer running SMTO. SMTO couldn't open it, usually because something else is already using that address. Nothing was sent to Microsoft.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you started a Microsoft sign-in in the last ten minutes, finish it in the browser tab you opened, or wait ten minutes for it to expire. An unfinished sign-in keeps the local return page open, so a second one can't use the same address.
  2. Close any other program on the computer running SMTO that might use the same address, such as another sign-in tool or a development server. Only one program at a time can use that address on the computer.
  3. Ask the Agent again to connect your Microsoft 365 account. Once the address is free, it's safe to start a new sign-in.

What success looks like

  • The Agent gives you a Microsoft sign-in link, and after you approve it the browser page says your account is connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; they may need to pick another local port for the Microsoft app registration. Don't change the app's tenant or secret to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • BrowserOAuth.start could not bind the loopback callback listener on 127.0.0.1 at the port of the public Microsoft OAuth App's redirect_uri (OSError on bind), so no consent request was created.

What this means

  • Browser OAuth cannot bind its required callback listener and maps the listener error through the Microsoft adapter. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Browser OAuth cannot bind its required callback listener and maps the listener error through the Microsoft adapter.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the registered callback address and actual bind failure or occupied port.

How to fix it

  • Find what holds the redirect_uri port on the SMTO server (default 8400, e.g. ss -ltnp | grep 8400): often an earlier pending connect whose listener stays up for up to ten minutes, or another program. Free the port, or register a different localhost port in Entra and set the same redirect_uri on the Microsoft OAuth App in Parameter Store, then call microsoft365.connect again.
  • Restore the registered callback listener address/port, then start a new supported connect flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported listener starts on the registered callback before new consent.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
